editorial: Today, there is a technically focused concentration on browser-based autonomous agents (agent-browser) and the security architectures of artificial intelligence models. New language models on Hugging Face and data integrity studies in RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) processes provide critical resources for making systems more reliable.

items.title: vercel-labs/agent-browser
items.summary: Developed by Vercel Labs, agent-browser is a command-line interface (CLI) that allows artificial intelligence agents to perform operations in a browser. This tool reads pages as an accessibility tree, enabling agents to interact with web elements.

snapshot.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents. Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

items.title: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
items.summary: Developed by Cloudflare, security-audit-skill is a skill package that transforms coding agents used in software development processes into security auditors. This tool performs multi-stage security audits, from discovery to reporting, with independently verifiable and machine-readable findings.

snapshot.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings. A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

items.title: google/skills
items.summary: Shared by Google, google/skills offers artificial intelligence skill packages developed for technologies such as Google products and Google Cloud. This Python-based repository aims to standardize the interaction of artificial intelligence agents with services in the Google ecosystem.

snapshot.description: Agent Skills for Google products and technologies. This repository contains Agent Skills for Google products and technologies, including Google Cloud.

items.title: mattpocock/skills
items.summary: Mattpocock/skills is a collection containing artificial intelligence agent skills used by software engineers in their daily workflows. Focusing on automating real engineering tasks, this resource aims to support functional coding processes rather than trial-and-error methods.

snapshot.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory. My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding.

items.title: anthropics/skills
items.summary: Shared by Anthropic, skills contains various skill packages showcasing the capabilities of the Claude artificial intelligence system. Developed in Python, this repository offers a wide range of use cases, from creative applications to technical tasks and enterprise workflows.

snapshot.description: Public repository for Agent Skills. This repository contains skills that demonstrate what's possible with Claude's skills system. These skills range from creative applications (art, music, design) to technical tasks (testing web apps, MCP server generation) to enterprise workflows (communications, branding, etc.).

items.title: meta/astryx
items.summary: Developed by Meta, astryx is a fully customizable open-source design system designed for use by both humans and artificial intelligence agents. Prepared in TypeScript, this system aims to support human and artificial intelligence collaboration in modern software development processes.

snapshot.description: An open source design system that's fully customizable and agent ready. An open source design system that's fully customizable and built for how we build now: by people and the agents working alongside them.

items.title: prometheus/prometheus
items.summary: Prometheus is an open-source monitoring system that provides system and service monitoring along with time series database management. As a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project, this software collects metrics from defined targets, evaluates rules, and triggers alerts when defined conditions are met.

snapshot.description: The Prometheus monitoring system and time series database. Prometheus, a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project, is a systems and service monitoring system. It collects metrics from configured targets at given intervals, evaluates rule expressions, displays the results, and can trigger alerts when specified conditions are observed.

items.title: sherlock-project/sherlock
items.summary: Developed in Python, sherlock-project/sherlock is a tool that scans for social media accounts across different networks using usernames. The project offers community-maintained package support for various platforms such as Debian, Ubuntu, Homebrew, Kali, and BlackArch.

snapshot.description: Hunt down social media accounts by username across social networks. Community-maintained packages are available for Debian (>= 13), Ubuntu (>= 22.10), Homebrew, Kali, and BlackArch. These packages are not directly supported or maintained by the Sherlock Project.

items.title: milind-soni/OpenMausBot
items.summary: OpenMausBot is an open-source Grok Bot alternative that allows you to create your own artificial intelligence bot teams within chat applications. The system expands its functionality by providing a virtual machine infrastructure that bots can use.

snapshot.description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative with a virtual machine that bots can use. The open-source Grok Bot alternative: your own team of AI bots, in a chat app.

items.title: astral-sh/ruff
items.summary: Ruff is a fast Python linter and code formatter developed in the Rust programming language. It is used in software development processes to check the compliance of Python projects with standards and to accelerate code formatting tasks.

snapshot.description: An extremely fast Python linter and code formatter, written in Rust. An extremely fast Python linter and code formatter, written in Rust.

items.title: tailwindlabs/tailwindcss
items.summary: Tailwind CSS is a utility-first CSS framework focused on rapid user interface development. It provides predefined classes to accelerate the design process in web projects.

snapshot.description: A utility-first CSS framework for rapid UI development. For help, discussion about best practices, or feature ideas:

items.title: mbillow/localthings
items.summary: mbillow/localthings allows you to control Samsung home appliances with the smart home management platform Home Assistant over a local network without requiring a cloud account. Developed in Python, this tool moves control over your devices directly to your local network.

snapshot.description: Control your Samsung appliances from Home Assistant over your home network, with no cloud account. Control your Samsung appliances from Home Assistant over your home network, with no cloud account.

items.title: zed-industries/zed
items.summary: Zed is a high-performance, multiplayer code editor built in Rust by the developers of Atom and Tree-sitter. Aiming to accelerate software development processes, this tool offers the ability to work simultaneously.

snapshot.description: Code at the speed of thought – Zed is a high-performance, multiplayer code editor from the creators of Atom and Tree-sitter.

items.title: ranxianglei/billion-context
items.summary: Developed with TypeScript, billion-context is a compression plugin that works on the context window, which refers to the information capacity that AI models can process at once. This tool aims to reduce token usage by five times by fitting billions of tokens into smaller spaces during long monthly sessions.

snapshot.description: A context-compression plugin for month-long single sessions (billions of tokens) ,small context windows (a 100K context is enough) and token savings (5x fewer tokens) .上下文压缩插件，月级长会话会话， 兼顾小窗口(100k上下文足矣)省token(省5倍token) . billion-context is all you need

items.title: dsx-ai-factory/nvke
items.summary: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) provides a management plane that enables the management of GPU-accelerated Kubernetes clusters on bare metal servers. Developed in Go, this tool runs on Docker infrastructure with virtual TPM support, simplifying cluster setup and workload creation processes.

snapshot.description: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE). A management plane for GPU Kubernetes on bare metal. The local quickstart runs on a Linux host or VM, amd64 or arm64, with at least 6 CPUs, 12 GiB of free memory and 100 GiB of free disk. It requires Docker, virtual TPM support and the tools listed in the guide. Follow its setup through workload-cluster creation and confirm the cluster's nodes report Ready.

items.title: Need for Speed Underground 2 online in the browser
items.summary: Need for Speed Underground 2 has been made playable via a browser using WebGPU technology. This fan-developed project offers 120 FPS support, widescreen mode, and online racing capabilities.

snapshot.description: Play Need for Speed: Underground 2 (2004) in Chrome and Firefox with WebGPU graphics, Web Audio, up to 120 fps widescreen, controller support, free roam and Online races with friends. Fan project, not affiliated with Electronic Arts.

items.title: Every Mac comes with an (undocumented) family member classifier
items.summary: An undocumented family member classifier found on Apple devices is used to create a personal knowledge graph. This feature provides a structure that identifies family relationships by analyzing user data within the scope of Apple Intelligence.

items.title: What I run on my $10 USD OpenStick homelab
items.summary: A homelab set up on a ten-dollar OpenStick device demonstrates how low-cost hardware can be used for server functions. This setup offers the opportunity to experience methods for building personal digital infrastructure on a limited budget.

snapshot.description: What I run on my $10 USD OpenStick homelab

items.summary: The AI Frontiers group, operating under Microsoft Research, is being shut down. This development signals a restructuring of research activities within the tech giant Microsoft.

items.title: Apple’s grey list: Words and phrases your iPhone won’t help you spell
items.summary: Apple maintains a list of over 100,000 words and phrases that the predictive text feature is prevented from completing. These restrictions prevent the device from suggesting or automatically correcting specific word groups for the user.

snapshot.description: There are more than 100,000 words and phrases that the tech giant has restricted its predictive text from completing, research shows

items.title: speridlabs/idol
items.summary: speridlabs/idol is an AI model that creates a 3D Gaussian splat from a single image. By removing the background and framing the object, this tool outputs in the standard 3DGS .ply format and runs in under two seconds on consumer-grade graphics processors.

snapshot.description: image-to-3d model. Idol turns one picture of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat. Give it a render, a generated image or a photo: it removes the background, frames the object and generates up to 1,048,576 Gaussians, written as a standard 3DGS .ply. It runs on consumer GPUs, using 7.2 GB of VRAM and can run in under 2 seconds.

items.title: moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro
items.summary: Kimi-K3.1-Pro, developed by Moonshot AI, is a multimodal AI model capable of processing visual and text data. Trained on top of the Kimi K3 model using large-scale reinforcement learning methods, this model is presented as the first and most capable version of the K3.1 series.

snapshot.description: image-text-to-text model. Kimi K3.1 Pro is an open-weight, natively multimodal agentic model, and our most capable 3T-class model to date. Post-trained from Kimi K3 with large-scale joint reinforcement learning across hundreds of downstream domains, it is the first model in the K3.1 series.

items.title: xtools-at/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Qwen3.5-9B-UNCENSORED-heretic
items.summary: xtools-at/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Qwen3.5-9B-UNCENSORED-heretic is presented as an AI model focused on text generation. Showing an average success rate of 94.50 percent on vLLM in GSM8K tests, the model aims to approach the performance of larger models with its 9B parameter size.

snapshot.description: text-generation model. The NVFP4 checkpoint was evaluated on GSM8K four times, and the resulting scores were averaged. Its four-run mean accuracy is 94.50% under vLLM. In the comparison supplied with this release, the 9B student slightly exceeds the reported DeepSeek-V4-Pro teacher result and approaches the Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct reference.

items.title: ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder
items.summary: ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder, shared on Hugging Face, is an experiment examining the feasibility of small language models in general-purpose coding and high-quality 3D scene generation processes. With a limited number of parameters, the model aims to perform in both software development and visual content production fields.

snapshot.description: An experiment exploring the feasibility of small language models for general-purpose coding and high-quality 3D scene generation.

items.title: Lightricks/LTX-2.5
items.summary: LTX-2.5, developed by Lightricks, is an image-to-video artificial intelligence model that transforms images into moving footage. It offers a technology that allows users to move their static content into a video format.

snapshot.description: image-to-video model

items.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
items.summary: The article 'Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents' proposes that large language model (LLM) agents process tool outputs using latent context compression instead of text. This approach aims to reduce the context load caused by processing long and noisy data as text, allowing agents to better focus on task-oriented information.

snapshot.description: Large language model (LLM) agents typically append raw tool outputs to their context. Over multi-step interactions, long and noisy observations incur substantial context overhead and dilute the agent's attention to task-relevant information. Existing token pruning and summarization methods remain constrained by discrete text representations, limiting the achievable compression ratios. In this work, we challenge the prevailing assumption that agents must consume tool observations as explicit text

items.title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: The article shared by Hugging Face examines the text and vector integrity gap in offline RAG (a method that enables AI to generate answers by retrieving information from your current and private data) processes used on edge devices. Addressing the vulnerability of signed information packets to vector manipulation, the study analyzes security gaps in verification mechanisms and how these gaps can be exploited by attackers.

snapshot.description: Offline retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on edge devices is updated through signed knowledge packs that carry text and precomputed embedding vectors. A signature proves who published a pack, not that its vectors encode its text. We study this text-vector integrity gap. A verifier that recomputes vectors and accepts them within a cosine tolerance concedes a predictable share of queries to an attacker who controls the vectors: the hijack rate equals the distribution of angular retrieval margin

items.title: StepX-OPD: Rethinking Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Diffusion Models
items.summary: StepX-OPD re-examines the multi-teacher on-policy distillation process in text-to-image diffusion models. The study investigates performance losses in the two-stage training process required for the model to perform few-step sampling while maintaining its capabilities.

snapshot.description: A deployable text-to-image diffusion model must hold several capabilities at once, such as instruction following, text rendering and human preference, and must sample in a few steps. Capabilities and few-step sampling are built in separate stages: a full-step model first consolidates capabilities through multi-teacher on-policy distillation, then serves as a fixed teacher for step distillation. items.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
items.summary: SwarmEvolve is a framework aimed at accelerating large language model (LLM)-based evolutionary search processes used in solving mathematical and computational problems. By using hundreds of low-cost agents in a swarm, it provides optimization through reasoning in latent space instead of text generation.

snapshot.description: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decod

items.title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
items.summary: OpenFrontiers, published on Hugging Face, is an interdisciplinary resource and benchmark set containing scientific research problems and recently solved mathematical issues. It offers a structured data pool to evaluate the research-level problem-solving capabilities of large language models (LLMs).

snapshot.description: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in research-level problem solving, yet a comprehensive collection of such problems is still missing, and evaluating them on research-level problems remains challenging. We introduce OpenFrontiers, a cross-disciplinary resource that combines a structured corpus of open research problems with a retrospective benchmark of recently resolved problems in mathematics. glossary.explanation: A text-based interface that allows you to manage programs by writing written commands instead of using a mouse.
A data structure that presents the structure and function of elements on web pages in a hierarchical order that AIs or screen readers can understand.
Artificial intelligence software that automatically performs coding, debugging, or editing tasks in software development processes.
The set of specific functions and capabilities that artificial intelligence agents need to perform certain tasks.
A type of software whose source code is open for anyone to inspect, modify, and improve.
A special type of database that stores timestamped data for the purpose of tracking and analyzing changes.
A software-based computer environment that runs its own operating system using the resources of a physical computer.
An inspection tool that automatically scans and reports faulty or non-standard parts of written code.
A tool that automatically aligns the appearance and layout of written code according to predetermined rules.
A method that accelerates interface development by presenting design styles in small, single-function pieces.
A ready-made code library that allows you to create the visual design of web pages faster and more systematically.
An application used by developers while writing code, featuring advanced capabilities such as text editing and debugging.
The limit on the amount of data that artificial intelligence models can remember and process simultaneously during an operation.
The smallest unit of data, corresponding to words or character fragments, used by artificial intelligence models when processing text.
A control platform offered by NVIDIA used to manage GPU-accelerated server clusters.
A physical server that does not have a virtualization layer and is installed directly onto the hardware.
